title: Advanced Debounce with Leading, Trailing & Cancel Controls
problemStatement: Implement `debounceAdvanced(fn, delay, { leading = false, trailing = true })`. Provide `.cancel()` to abort any pending execution and `.flush()` to immediately execute any pending call.
interviewTrap: If `leading: true` and `trailing: false`, the function fires immediately, but must NOT fire at the end of the delay window.

testCases.name: Supports leading execution immediately
testCases.input: leading: true fires immediately on first call
testCases.testFn: let count = 0; const debounced = debounceAdvanced(() => count++, 50, { leading: true, trailing: false }); debounced(); return count;

testCases.name: cancel() aborts pending delayed execution
testCases.testFn: let count = 0; const debounced = debounceAdvanced(() => count++, 30); debounced(); debounced.cancel(); await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 45)); return count;

testCases.name: flush() triggers pending execution synchronously
testCases.testFn: let count = 0; const debounced = debounceAdvanced(() => count++, 50); debounced(); debounced.flush(); return count;

interviewCrossQuestions.question: Why does a production debounce function need .cancel() and .flush() methods?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: `.cancel()` cleans up pending timers when components unmount (preventing memory leaks and state updates on unmounted components). `.flush()` forces immediate execution of any pending deferred call (essential on form submission or navigation before timers expire).
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests production-grade lifecycle integration (the Lodash pattern).

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What is maxWait in Lodash debounce?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: `maxWait` guarantees that a continuously triggered debounced function will still be forced to execute at least once every `maxWait` milliseconds, preventing indefinite execution starvation during nonstop typing.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests deep familiarity with industry-standard utility libraries.

howToExplain.opening: A production-grade debounce combines leading/trailing triggers with explicit lifecycle controls (.cancel, .flush) and starvation limits (maxWait).
keyPoints: Supports leading execution for immediate feedback and trailing for final state capture.
.cancel() prevents memory leaks on component unmount.
maxWait prevents continuous event streams from postponing execution indefinitely.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Advanced debounce is not just a timer utility; it is a full lifecycle state machine.
analogies: An emergency door release: it normally waits for authorization, but the fire alarm (.flush) opens it immediately, and the power switch (.cancel) disarms it.

commonMistakes.mistake: Forgetting to clear timer references inside .cancel().
commonMistakes.why: Leaving the timer ID uncleared can cause stale checks or prevent garbage collection.
commonMistakes.correct: Call clearTimeout(timer) and reset timer = null.

followUpDeepDive.question: How does Lodash share code between debounce and throttle?
followUpDeepDive.answer: In Lodash source code, `throttle` is actually implemented directly on top of `debounce` by simply passing `{ leading: true, trailing: true, maxWait: wait }` to the debounce engine.
